A1=Long Term Growth Model (LTGM) Spreadsheet

A3=2021-12-16 00:00:00

A8=Comments and suggestions welcome, please email Steven Pennings (spennings@worldbank.org) or LTGM@worldbank.org
A9=The spreadsheet updated regularly, please check back LTGM website (below) for the last version:
A10=http://www.worldbank.org/LTGM
A11=Based on the model by Hevia and Loayza (2012) "Savings and Growth in Egypt" Middle East Development Journal 4 (1)
A12=Thanks to Vinaya Swaroop for project overview and Diego Barrot for assistance with data 

A14=See the pdf "Long Term Growth Model V4_3" for a list of model equations, and an explanation of the drivers of growth in the LTGM.
A15=System Requirements:  | C15=if using Excel 2010 or later all features work as planned*
C16=if using earlier versions of Excel, dropdown menus are not supported; but there is an easy fix - see instruction (7) below
C17=There are no macros in this spreadsheet
A18=New in v4 -  poverty extension. Now users can see the implications of growth fundamentals for poverty rates. See Model description Section 5 for a description

A20=1) General Instructions
A21=Worksheet "InputDataA_GeneralAssumptions" controls most simulation parameters and assumptions that affect all three models
A22=Choose your country from the drop down menu at the top left of "InputDataA_GeneralAssumptions" (select the cell first).
A23=Data from that country will automatically be populated, but you can specify most of the parameters yourself if you choose (see Worksheet "GraphsA" figures of general assumptions).
A24=Worksheet "InputDataB_ModelSpecAssumptions" controls model-specific parameters
A25=If you want to calculate growth for a given investment-to-GDP profile, use Model 1
A26=If you want to calculate required investment to achieve a target growth path, use Model 2
A27=If you want to calculate growth for a given savings-to-GDP profile, use Model 3 
A28=(This this last case also requires some assumption on external balance, described below)
A29=See  Worksheet "GrapshB" for graphs of model-specific inputs and outputs
A30=Color coding:  | B30=Yellow= can edit | D30=Grey=not active (don’t edit) | G30=Red = formulas/populated data (don't edit)

A32=2) Entering General Parameter Assumptions (use InputDataA_GeneralAssumptions)
A33=In most cases you can choose  "automatic"  or "manual" version of each series from a drop-down menu
A34=- if automatic, select a target value and the year it is achieved and the spreadsheet automatically generates a smooth path to get there
A35=- if manual, you must type the values manually into the ""Manual" [user defined year by year]" yellow cells to the right in InputDataA and InputDataB (they become yellow when you select manual from the drop down menu)
A36=Model 1, 2 and 3 uses the same general parameters as each other; Model 1s, 2s and 3s uses the same general parameters as each other("s" is for scenarios -  see below)
A37=The parameters which actually go into the calculations are listed in "Summary of Inputs based on User's choice"  in the  Model 1(s),  Model 2(s) and  Model 3(s) spreadsheets

A39=3) Entering Model 1-, Model 2- or Model 3-specific parameters - Use InputDataB sheet
A40=For Model 1, choose either "automated" or "manual" values for a path of I/Y (as above), these will not affect Model 2 or 3
A41=For Model 2, choose between the types of growth target: a GDP per capita growth target, a headline GDP growth target,  a GDP per capita levels target (does not affect Model 1 or 3)
A42=  - Then choose between  "automated" or "manual" values for a path of the growth target. If automatic, you also need to choose an end date as above and the model generates a smooth path
A43=  - If choose "manual" then you need to enter the values corresponding to the type of growth target in InputDataB on the RHS row 13 and 19. Eg  5000  (for a GDP per capita levels target) or 0.06 (for a growth target)
A44=     - The model automatically interprets the "type" of these numbers, and converts them to an implied GDP per capita growth target the Model 2 and Model 2s sheets
A45=For Model 3, choose either "automated" or "manual" values for a path of S/Y (as above), these will not affect Model 1 or 2

A47=4) Changing initial assumptions, simulation years and other parameters
A48=By default, initial values are calibrated as historical averages from various data sources (or taken from most recent year).
A49=The user can change the first year of the simulation in the "Initial year for estimation" cell (top LHS of "input dataA"). For years up to 2018, we forecast starting values (see comment sticky notes in the input data sheet for details).
A50=However, the user doesn't have to choose these starting values as the initial values for automatic paths
A51= - to choose a different starting value, enter it it in the yellow cell next to "Initial value (user defined)"
A52= - to use the historical average (from data) or most recent historical  data just keep the "Initial value (user defined)" BLANK
A53= - a summary of the actual initial value used (user defined or historical average) indicated in red
A54=The user is also able to specify alterantive depreciation rates, initial K/Y or labor share in a similar way in the top LHS of the input sheet.
A55=The initial value of real GDP per capita does not affect the operation of the model (which is all in growth rates) but does affect memorandum items. It can be set at the top LHS of the "InputDataA_GeneralAssumptions".

A57=5) External Balance Constraints
A58=The user can choose two types of constraints on the external sector (via a dropdown menu): Current Account Balance /Y or External Debt/Y
A59=-- These govern the relationship beteen S/Y and I/Y, which are particularly important for Model 3
A60=For the CAB/Y constraint, choose either manual or automatic via the drop down menu.
A61= - for countries with a closed capital account, simply choose a current account balance constraint, and then set it equal to zero. Then S=I for all periods.
A62=For the external debt/Y constraint, choose either manual or automatic via the drop down menu.
A63= - for the external debt/Y option, the user also needs to choose an FDI/Y path (manual or automatic) -- this is not required for a current account balance/Y constraint
A64= - if automatic paths the user can also choose choose the final target, date reached, and also an initial value (
A65= - if manual, enter the paths for each year in the yellow cells on the RHS of InputDataA

A67=6) Baseline vs Scenarios
A68=There are two versions of each Model: a "baseline" version (the main one) and a "scenario" version (labelled "s")
A69=Scenarios allows you to easily compare two outputs given different assumptions in the "GraphsA" and "GraphsB" worksheet
B70=For example, to calculate growth rates given the same investment profile but different TFP growth assumptions, use Model 1 for one (baseline) TFP assumption, and Model 1s (scenario) for the alternative TFP assumption.

A72=Model 1, 2, 3 apply to the "baseline". Model 1s, 2s, 3s apply to the "scenarios". Automatic and Manual (from the drop-down menu) apply to both Baseline and Scenario
A73=   - this means if you set a series to manual, you need to manually type in those values into "User defined, year by year" yellow cells in worksheet "InputDataA_ GeneralAssumptions" or "InputDataB_ModelSpecAssumptions" for both baseline and scenario
A74=These switch to yellow (user able to edit) when you chose manual from the dropdown menu.

A76=7) Instruction specfic for pre-Excel 2010 versions
A77=In pre-2010 versions of Excel the dropdown menus don't work. But this is easy to fix by manually typing the values instead (making sure spelling is exact). Worksheet: InputDataA_ GeneralAssumptions 
A78=Country Name InputDataA_ GeneralAssumptions B3)
A79=- lookup your country name in data>Cells B23+ edit the cell and copy the text of the country name in the edit bar at the top of the screen (DO NOT copy the cell, just the text - you will need unhide the "data" worksheet)
A80=- edit InputDataA_ GeneralAssumptions>B3, and paste the name of county text into the edit bar at the top of the screen
A81=- alternatively, just Type the Country name into InputDataA_ GeneralAssumptions>B3, making sure that the Country name is spelt correctly
A82=Automatic vs Manual (Inputdata: Various Cells)
A83=- Type "Automatic" or "Manual" (without quotes) to run that series in Automatic or Manual mode
A84=External balance 
A85=- Type "Debt" or "CAB" (without quotes) InputDataA_ GeneralAssumptions>D60 to choose the type of external debt constraint
A86=Output Target (Model 2 and 2s Only)
A87=- Type "GDP Growth" or "GDP PC Growth" or "GDP PC Level" (without quotes) InputDataB_ ModelSpecAssumptions>D20 to choose the type of output target when using Model 2 or 2s

A89=* in testing, occationally conditonal formatting would only update when one changed to a different tab.
